The test image shows a corn leaf with several elongated, rectangular, tan/brown lesions that appear constrained between leaf veins. This is a **leaf** disease.

Top candidates from leaf classes: Gray_Leaf_Spot, Northern_Leaf_Blight, Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight, Goss_S_Wilt, Carbonum_Leaf_Spot, Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Stewart_S_Disease, Eyespot.

Let me view one reference from each top candidate.
Gray Leaf Spot reference shows rectangular, vein-bounded lesions - similar pattern. Let me check other candidates.
NLB lesions are much larger and cigar-shaped - doesn't match. Let me check more candidates.
SCLB also shows rectangular vein-bounded lesions - similar. Let me check more candidates.
Goss's Wilt shows large, water-soaked, blighted areas - very different from the test image. Not a match.
Carbonum shows many small circular spots - not matching. Let me check more.
Stewart's shows long continuous streaks - different from the discrete rectangular lesions in test image.
Anthracnose shows irregular edge lesions with dark margins - different. My top two are Gray_Leaf_Spot and Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight. Let me use my last view to compare.

Both GLS references confirm the match. The test image shows discrete, rectangular, tan lesions clearly bounded by leaf veins, which is the hallmark of Gray Leaf Spot. The lesions are narrow, elongated between veins, and tan-colored, consistent with both GLS references. SCLB lesions tend to be smaller with more prominent reddish-brown margins. NLB lesions are much larger and cigar-shaped. The other candidates (Goss's Wilt, Stewart's, Carbonum, Anthracnose) all showed distinctly different patterns.
